name: Fire & Special Perils
description: Covers physical damage to buildings, equipment, and stock from fire, lightning, explosion, storm, flood, and other specified perils.
claim_examples: A fire in a factory warehouse destroyed ₦15M worth of raw materials
A storm caused roof damage to a retail store, closing it for 3 weeks
An electrical surge triggered a fire that damaged ₦8M in office equipment

objections.objection: We've never had a fire in 10 years
objections.response: Many business owners say the same until it happens. Fire risk increases with electrical age, and most Nigerian businesses don't have adequate electrical inspections. The question isn't whether you'll have a fire—it's whether you can afford to rebuild without insurance.

objections.objection: Insurance is too expensive
objections.response: Fire insurance typically costs 0.1-0.5% of your sum insured per year. For a ₦50M facility, that's ₦50,000-₦250,000 annually. Compare that to the cost of rebuilding without insurance.

proposal_template: We recommend Fire & Special Perils insurance to protect your {{assets}} against fire, storm, flood, and other specified risks. Estimated premium: ₦{{minPremium}} - ₦{{maxPremium}} annually.

faqs.q: Does Fire & Special Perils cover earthquakes?
faqs.a: Standard Nigerian policies cover earthquakes under Special Perils, but confirm with your insurer.

faqs.q: Can I insure just my building without contents?
faqs.a: Yes, you can insure building only, contents only, or both.

faqs.q: What is the typical excess on a fire policy?
faqs.a: Most Nigerian insurers apply a 5-10% excess on fire claims, subject to a minimum of ₦50,000.

name: Fire & Burglary
description: Combined cover for small and medium enterprises protecting premises, stock, and equipment against fire, theft, burglary, and armed robbery.
common_risks: Night burglary of stock and cash
exclusions: Fraudulent or dishonest acts of directors
Goods held on consignment unless declared
claim_examples: A pharmacy in Surulere lost ₦3.2M in drugs and cash during an overnight burglary
A restaurant kitchen fire caused ₦1.8M damage to cooking equipment and stock

objections.objection: We have security guards, so we don't need burglary cover
objections.response: Security guards help deter crime but cannot prevent all incidents. In 2023, over 60% of businesses with guards still experienced theft. Insurance covers the loss your guards couldn't prevent.

objections.objection: Our shop is small, it won't happen to us
objections.response: Small shops are actually more vulnerable—they often have weaker security infrastructure. The average burglary claim for SMEs in Nigeria is ₦850,000. Can your business absorb that loss?

proposal_template: We recommend Fire & Burglary cover for your {{businessType}} to protect against fire damage and theft. Estimated premium: ₦{{minPremium}} - ₦{{maxPremium}} annually.

faqs.q: Is cash kept overnight covered under burglary?
faqs.a: Cash is covered up to a specified limit (usually 10% of sum insured, max ₦100,000). Higher limits require separate cash insurance.

faqs.q: Does this cover employee theft?
faqs.a: No, employee dishonesty requires a separate Fidelity Guarantee policy.

name: Public Liability
description: Protects your business against legal liability for third-party bodily injury or property damage arising from your business operations.
who_needs_it: Any business that deals with the public
common_risks: Customer slips and falls on premises
Property damage caused to third parties
Injury to members of the public
exclusions: Products after delivery (covered by Product Liability)
Contractual liabilities beyond standard duty of care
claim_examples: A customer slipped on a wet floor in a supermarket and broke their leg, claiming ₦2.5M in damages
A construction company's crane dropped debris on a neighboring car, causing ₦1.2M in damage

objections.objection: We are careful, nothing will happen
objections.response: Most liability claims are accidents, not negligence. A customer slipping on a wet floor or a falling display shelf can happen despite the best precautions. Legal costs alone for defending a claim can exceed ₦1M.

objections.objection: Our business is online only, we don't have foot traffic
objections.response: You may still need liability cover for premises you visit (client offices, co-working spaces) and for products you sell. Product liability is often bundled.

proposal_template: We recommend Public Liability insurance for {{businessName}} with a limit of ₦{{limit}}. This covers third-party bodily injury and property damage arising from your {{operations}}. Estimated premium: ₦{{minPremium}} - ₦{{maxPremium}} annually.

faqs.q: What is a typical liability limit for SMEs?
faqs.a: Most SMEs in Nigeria take ₦5M to ₦25M in public liability cover. Larger businesses may need ₦50M+.

faqs.q: Does Public Liability cover legal fees?
faqs.a: Yes, legal defense costs are covered in addition to the liability limit, up to a specified amount.

name: Employers Liability
description: Covers your legal liability for bodily injury or disease sustained by employees in the course of their employment, as required by the Nigerian Employees Compensation Act.
who_needs_it: Companies with manual or hazardous labor
exclusions: Injuries outside work hours and premises
claim_examples: A factory worker lost two fingers in a press machine, awarded ₦3.8M under the Employees Compensation Act
A delivery driver was injured in a road accident while making company deliveries, claim settled at ₦1.5M

objections.objection: My staff are like family, I take care of them
objections.response: That's commendable, but the Employees Compensation Act requires all employers to carry this insurance. Without it, you're personally liable for workplace injuries, and NAICOM can impose penalties of up to ₦500,000.

objections.objection: We only have office staff, no manual work
objections.response: Even office workers face risks—slips, trips, falls, repetitive strain injuries, and even stress-related claims. The law applies to all employees regardless of role.

proposal_template: We recommend Employers Liability insurance for {{companyName}} to cover all {{employeeCount}} employees against workplace injuries and occupational diseases as required by law. Estimated premium: ₦{{minPremium}} - ₦{{maxPremium}} annually.

faqs.q: Is Employers Liability mandatory in Nigeria?
faqs.a: Yes, under the Employees Compensation Act 2010, all employers must provide this cover or face penalties.

faqs.q: What is the minimum sum insured per employee?
faqs.a: The act requires a minimum of ₦1M per employee, though higher limits are recommended.

name: Goods in Transit
description: Covers loss or damage to goods while being transported by road, rail, air, or courier within Nigeria.
common_risks: Fire damage to goods in transit
claim_examples: A truck carrying ₦6.5M worth of electronics was hijacked along the Lagos-Ibadan expressway
A consignment of ₦2.3M in pharmaceutical products was destroyed when the delivery van caught fire

objections.objection: Our drivers are careful and our vehicles are reliable
objections.response: You can control your drivers but not the other vehicles on the road, armed robbers, or sudden accidents. Just last year, cargo theft along Nigerian highways accounted for ₦48B in losses.

objections.objection: We transfer the risk to the transporter
objections.response: Transporter liability is often limited and difficult to enforce. A dedicated Goods in Transit policy ensures you're directly compensated without relying on the transporter's insurance.

proposal_template: We recommend Goods in Transit insurance for {{businessName}} covering goods valued up to ₦{{sumInsured}} during transportation within Nigeria. Estimated premium: ₦{{minPremium}} - ₦{{maxPremium}} annually.

faqs.q: Is goods in transit the same as marine cargo?
faqs.a: No. Goods in Transit covers domestic road/rail transport, while Marine Cargo covers cross-border and international shipments.

faqs.q: Can I insure goods on a per-trip basis?
faqs.a: Yes, we offer both annual policies and per-declaration (open cover) policies for flexible shipping volumes.

name: Group Personal Accident
description: Provides financial compensation to employees or their families in case of accidental death, permanent disability, or temporary disablement.
who_needs_it: Employers who want to protect their workforce
common_risks: Loss of income due to accident
exclusions: Injuries from war or civil commotion
claim_examples: An employee suffered permanent loss of sight in one eye from a workplace chemical splash, receiving ₦4M in compensation
A staff member was paralyzed from the waist down in a road accident, policy paid ₦10M lump sum

objections.objection: We already have NHIS for our staff
objections.response: NHIS covers medical treatment, not income replacement or lump-sum compensation. Group Personal Accident pays your staff (or their family) cash if they are injured or die—medical cover alone is not enough.

objections.objection: It's an extra cost we don't need
objections.response: For as little as ₦5,000 per employee per year, you provide a ₦5M+ benefit. It's one of the most appreciated and cost-effective staff benefits you can offer.

proposal_template: We recommend Group Personal Accident cover for {{companyName}} insuring {{employeeCount}} employees against accidental death and disability. Estimated premium: ₦{{minPremium}} - ₦{{maxPremium}} annually.

faqs.q: Does this cover road accidents outside work?
faqs.a: Yes, most group personal accident policies provide 24-hour cover, including travel to and from work.

faqs.q: What is the typical sum insured per employee?
faqs.a: Sum insured typically ranges from ₦2M to ₦10M per employee, depending on role and seniority.

name: Business Interruption
description: Replaces lost income and covers ongoing expenses when your business cannot operate due to an insured event like fire, flood, or equipment breakdown.
who_needs_it: Any business that would struggle to survive a shutdown
claim_examples: A bakery fire shut down operations for 6 weeks, BI claim paid ₦8.2M for lost profits and fixed costs
A factory flood required 4 weeks of repairs, BI policy covered ₦12M in revenue loss and ₦3.5M in extra costs

objections.objection: We have fire insurance, that's enough
objections.response: Fire insurance covers rebuilding your factory, but what about the income you lose while rebuilding? Most businesses that suffer a major loss and lack BI cover never reopen. BI is what keeps you in business during recovery.

objections.objection: How do we calculate the sum insured?
objections.response: We base it on your annual gross profit and the estimated time needed to recover. Our team will help you calculate this—typically 12-24 months of gross profit plus ongoing expenses.

proposal_template: We recommend Business Interruption insurance for {{businessName}} with an indemnity period of {{months}} months, covering gross profit of up to ₦{{grossProfit}}. Estimated premium: ₦{{minPremium}} - ₦{{maxPremium}} annually.

faqs.q: How long does the indemnity period last?
faqs.a: Standard indemnity periods are 12, 18, or 24 months. Choose based on how long you expect it would take to restore operations.

faqs.q: Is Business Interruption standalone or bundled?
faqs.a: It is usually bundled with a material damage policy (like Fire & Special Perils). Some insurers offer it standalone.

name: Machinery Breakdown
description: Covers sudden and unforeseen physical damage to machinery, plant, and equipment from mechanical or electrical breakdown, human error, or operator negligence.
common_risks: Mechanical breakdown of engines and motors
Electrical breakdown of generators and switchgear
exclusions: Damage from fire (covered by Fire policy)
claim_examples: A bottling plant's filling machine suffered gearbox failure, repairs cost ₦9.8M, covered under MB policy
A textile manufacturer's generator armature burned out due to voltage fluctuation, claim paid ₦4.2M

objections.objection: We service our machines regularly, breakdowns won't happen
objections.response: Regular maintenance reduces but does not eliminate breakdown risk. Most breakdowns are caused by manufacturing defects, operator error, or unforeseen electrical faults—not lack of maintenance.

objections.objection: Our machines are still under warranty
objections.response: Manufacturer warranties typically expire after 1-2 years and don't cover operator error or electrical surges. Machinery Breakdown fills the gap after warranty expires and covers risks the warranty excludes.

proposal_template: We recommend Machinery Breakdown cover for {{businessName}} to protect {{equipmentCount}} critical machines and equipment. Estimated premium: ₦{{minPremium}} - ₦{{maxPremium}} annually.

faqs.q: Does this cover loss of production due to breakdown?
faqs.a: No, that requires Business Interruption cover. Machinery Breakdown only covers the cost of repairing or replacing the damaged machine.

faqs.q: Are mobile generators covered?
faqs.a: Yes, mobile and standby generators can be covered, provided their location and usage are declared.

name: Professional Indemnity
description: Covers legal liability for claims of professional negligence, errors, omissions, or breach of duty arising from the provision of professional services.
who_needs_it: IT service providers and software companies
common_risks: Failure to deliver professional services as contracted
exclusions: Claims arising before the policy inception
claim_examples: A patient sued a surgeon for ₦15M after a surgical complication led to permanent nerve damage
An engineering firm was sued for ₦8M when a structural design flaw caused a building defect

objections.objection: I have never been sued in 20 years of practice
objections.response: Medical and professional litigation is rising sharply in Nigeria. Even if the claim is frivolous, defending it costs ₦1M-₦3M in legal fees alone. Professional Indemnity covers both the award and your defense costs.

objections.objection: My professional body covers me
objections.response: Most professional bodies in Nigeria provide limited cover (often ₦1M-₦5M) which is inadequate for serious claims. A standalone policy gives you limits from ₦10M upwards and covers gaps the body's scheme may not.

proposal_template: We recommend Professional Indemnity insurance for {{profession}} {{practitionerName}} with a limit of ₦{{limit}} per claim. Estimated premium: ₦{{minPremium}} - ₦{{maxPremium}} annually.

faqs.q: Does Professional Indemnity cover defamation?
faqs.a: For some professions (media, PR), defamation can be included. For most professionals, it covers negligence and errors only—not defamation.

faqs.q: Is there a retroactive date exclusion?
faqs.a: Yes, policies typically exclude claims arising from work done before a specified retroactive date. Continuous cover is important to avoid gaps.

name: Contractors All Risk
description: Covers construction, erection, and civil engineering projects against physical loss or damage to the works, materials, equipment, and third-party liability during the construction period.
common_risks: Fire or storm damaging works under construction
Theft of building materials from site
Damage to plant and machinery on site
Third-party injury or property damage at site
exclusions: Normal wear and tear of construction equipment
War, riots, and civil commotion (can be added)
claim_examples: A storm collapsed scaffolding and damaged the building frame of a Lagos high-rise, claim paid ₦18.5M
Construction materials including ₦4.8M worth of steel rods were stolen from a site in Abuja

objections.objection: The main contractor has insurance, we don't need our own
objections.response: The main contractor's policy may not cover subcontractors or may have limits that don't fully protect your interest. Having your own CAR policy ensures you're independently protected.

objections.objection: Insurance will eat into our project margin
objections.response: CAR insurance typically costs 0.3-0.8% of the contract value. For a ₦100M project, that's ₦300,000-₦800,000. The cost of even one incident—theft, fire, or collapse—could wipe out your entire margin.

proposal_template: We recommend Contractors All Risk insurance for the {{projectName}} project valued at ₦{{contractValue}}. Cover includes works, materials, and third-party liability. Estimated premium: ₦{{minPremium}} - ₦{{maxPremium}}.

faqs.q: Does CAR insurance cover the maintenance period?
faqs.a: Yes, CAR policies typically include a 12-month maintenance period cover after completion.

faqs.q: Can we add delay in completion cover?
faqs.a: Yes, a Delay in Start-Up (DSU) extension is available to cover revenue loss if the project is delayed due to an insured event.

name: Comprehensive Motor Insurance
description: Full motor insurance covering damage to your vehicle, third-party liability, theft, fire, and vandalism. Also covers damage from accidents, floods, and other perils.
who_needs_it: Vehicle owners who want full protection
Owners of expensive or financed vehicles
exclusions: Wear and tear and mechanical breakdown
Tyres damaged by road conditions alone
Driving under the influence of alcohol/drugs
Vehicle used for unauthorized purposes (e.g., racing)
Claims during grace period if premium unpaid
claim_examples: A Toyota Camry was stolen in Lagos, comprehensive policy paid ₦9.2M (market value)
A bus belonging to a transport company was involved in a collision, repairs cost ₦3.8M

objections.objection: Third-party insurance is cheaper and mandatory
objections.response: Third-party only covers damage to others—not your vehicle. If your car is stolen or damaged in an accident, you get nothing. For a ₦5M car, comprehensive cover adds only ₦100,000-₦250,000 more per year than third-party.

objections.objection: I am a very careful driver
objections.response: Your driving skill doesn't prevent theft, vandalism, flooding, or being hit by an uninsured driver. Those are the risks comprehensive cover protects against.

proposal_template: We recommend Comprehensive Motor Insurance for your {{vehicleMake}} {{vehicleModel}} ({{year}}) valued at ₦{{vehicleValue}}. Estimated premium: ₦{{minPremium}} - ₦{{maxPremium}} annually.

faqs.q: What is the excess on motor comprehensive policies?
faqs.a: Standard excess is 2-5% of sum insured, minimum ₦25,000 for private vehicles and ₦50,000 for commercial vehicles.

faqs.q: Does comprehensive cover windscreen damage?
faqs.a: Yes, we can include windscreen and glass cover, typically with a separate lower excess of ₦5,000-₦10,000.

name: Group Life Assurance
description: Provides a lump sum payout to beneficiaries if an employee dies during the period of cover, whether due to natural causes, accident, or illness.
exclusions: Suicide within first 12 months (varies by insurer)
Death from pre-existing conditions not disclosed
claim_examples: An employee passed away from a heart attack, Group Life paid ₦5M to the nominated beneficiary
A staff member died in a road accident, family received ₦3M death benefit under the employer's scheme

objections.objection: We already have Group Personal Accident
objections.response: Group Personal Accident covers accidental death only. Group Life covers death from ALL causes including illness and natural causes. Most employers need both.

objections.objection: It's not mandatory for small businesses
objections.response: Actually, the Pension Reform Act and Employees Compensation Act require life cover for all employees. Beyond legal requirements, it's a low-cost way (₦5,000-₦15,000 per employee) to provide a meaningful benefit that families truly value.

proposal_template: We recommend Group Life Assurance for {{companyName}} covering {{employeeCount}} employees with a sum insured of ₦{{sumInsured}} per employee. Estimated premium: ₦{{minPremium}} - ₦{{maxPremium}} annually.

faqs.q: What is the minimum sum insured for Group Life?
faqs.a: There is no statutory minimum, but most insurers recommend at least 3-5 times annual salary per employee.

faqs.q: Can we add critical illness cover?
faqs.a: Yes, critical illness can be added as a rider, providing a lump sum if an employee is diagnosed with specified conditions like cancer or stroke.

name: Cyber Insurance
description: Covers financial losses, legal costs, and recovery expenses arising from data breaches, cyber attacks, ransomware, phishing, and other cyber incidents.
who_needs_it: Any business storing customer data digitally
exclusions: Acts of war or cyber warfare by nation states
Loss of value from intellectual property theft
Infrastructure failures not caused by cyber attack
claim_examples: A Lagos fintech company suffered a ransomware attack demanding $50,000 in Bitcoin, cyber policy covered ₦8.5M in recovery costs and ransom negotiation
An e-commerce platform had 50,000 customer records leaked, cyber insurance covered ₦4.2M in notification costs, credit monitoring, and regulatory fines

objections.objection: We have good IT security, we won't get hacked
objections.response: Even the best IT security cannot prevent all breaches. In 2023, 67% of Nigerian businesses experienced some form of cyber attack. Cyber insurance provides the financial safety net for when—not if—a breach occurs.

objections.objection: Cyber insurance is expensive
objections.response: For SMEs, cyber insurance starts at ₦100,000-₦300,000 per year for ₦10M-₦25M in cover. Compare that to the average cost of a data breach in Nigeria, which is ₦15M-₦50M including regulatory fines.

proposal_template: We recommend Cyber Insurance for {{businessName}} with coverage limits of ₦{{limit}} for data breach response, ransomware, and business interruption. Estimated premium: ₦{{minPremium}} - ₦{{maxPremium}} annually.

faqs.q: Does cyber insurance cover ransomware payments?
faqs.a: Most policies cover ransom payments (subject to sanctions screening) and include access to a breach response team and negotiators.

faqs.q: Is social engineering / phishing covered?
faqs.a: Yes, many policies now include social engineering fraud, covering losses from fraudulent transfer instructions.

faqs.q: What about NDPR fines?
faqs.a: Cyber insurance can cover NITDA/NDPR regulatory fines and defense costs arising from data breaches.

name: Marine Cargo Insurance
description: Covers loss of or damage to goods, merchandise, or cargo while being transported by sea, air, or land across international borders.
common_risks: Cargo damage from rough seas or storms
Cargo loss from vessel sinking or stranding
exclusions: Loss due to strikes or war (can be added)
Ordinary leakage or breakage in transit
claim_examples: A container of electronics from China was damaged by seawater ingress during the voyage, claim paid ₦12.8M
A shipment of textile materials destined for Kano was stolen from a Lagos warehouse before export, covered ₦6.5M

objections.objection: The shipping line covers our cargo
objections.response: Shipping lines have limited liability under international conventions—usually $500-$2,000 per package, regardless of your cargo's value. That's far below the actual value of most shipments.

objections.objection: We only import occasionally
objections.response: We offer single-trip policies for occasional shipments. For a small premium (0.3-0.8% of cargo value), you can protect each shipment individually without an annual commitment.

proposal_template: We recommend Marine Cargo insurance for {{businessName}} covering shipments valued up to ₦{{cargoValue}} on {{tradeRoute}} route. Estimated premium: ₦{{minPremium}} - ₦{{maxPremium}} per shipment or annually under open cover.

faqs.q: What is the difference between Institute Cargo Clauses A, B, and C?
faqs.a: Clause A provides all-risks cover (broadest), Clause B covers specified perils, and Clause C covers major perils only (most limited). We recommend Clause A for most shipments.

faqs.q: Can I insure goods on FOB versus CIF terms?
faqs.a: Yes, you can insure cargo regardless of Incoterms. The key is having insurable interest at the time of loss. We'll advise on the right point to attach cover.

name: Keyman Insurance
description: A life or critical illness policy on a key employee or director where the business is the beneficiary, protecting the company against financial loss if that person dies or becomes critically ill.
who_needs_it: Businesses dependent on a founder or director
Partnerships where one partner's death impacts the business
organizations with key salespeople or rainmakers
common_risks: Death of a founder or key executive
Critical illness of a key employee
Loss of clients and revenue after keyman departure
Cost of recruiting and training a replacement
claim_examples: The founder of a Lagos tech startup died suddenly, Keyman Insurance paid ₦25M to the company, enabling it to hire a CEO and continue operations
A lead engineer suffered a stroke and could no longer work, critical illness rider paid ₦15M to the company for recruitment and transition costs

objections.objection: We are a large company, no one person is irreplaceable
objections.response: Some roles take 6-12 months to replace effectively. During that gap, revenue can drop 30-50%. Keyman gives you the capital to bridge the gap, recruit, and stabilize. Every company has people they cannot afford to lose suddenly.

objections.objection: It's too expensive for a 'what if'
objections.response: Premiums for a 35-year-old keyman at ₦20M cover cost about ₦60,000-₦100,000 per year. If you lose that person for 6 months, your business could lose ₦10M+. Can you afford not to insure the person your business depends on?

proposal_template: We recommend Keyman Insurance for {{companyName}} on the life of {{keyPersonName}} for a sum assured of ₦{{sumAssured}}. The company is the beneficiary. Estimated premium: ₦{{minPremium}} - ₦{{maxPremium}} annually.

faqs.q: Who owns and pays for Keyman Insurance?
faqs.a: The business owns the policy, pays the premiums, and is the beneficiary. The key person's life is the insured life.

faqs.q: Is Keyman Insurance tax deductible?
faqs.a: Yes, premiums paid by the company are generally tax-deductible as a business expense, while the payout is tax-free.

name: Income Protection
description: Replaces a portion of an individual's income if they cannot work due to illness or injury, providing monthly payments until they can return to work or retire.
common_risks: Mental health conditions requiring time off
claim_examples: A surgeon was diagnosed with a hand tremor preventing surgery, income protection paid 75% of monthly income (₦850,000/month) for 18 months
A tech founder was diagnosed with severe depression requiring 6 months of treatment, policy paid ₦350,000/month during recovery

objections.objection: I have savings, I can survive a few months
objections.response: Most people's savings only last 3-6 months. If a serious illness keeps you out of work for 1-2 years, your savings will run out. Income Protection pays you monthly until you can return to work.

objections.objection: My NHIS covers medical treatment
objections.response: NHIS covers the cost of treatment, not your lost income. Even with free treatment, you still need to pay your rent, school fees, and daily expenses while unable to work.

proposal_template: We recommend Income Protection for {{clientName}} providing {{percentage}}% of monthly income (up to ₦{{monthlyBenefit}}) with a {{deferredPeriod}}-day waiting period. Estimated premium: ₦{{minPremium}} - ₦{{maxPremium}} annually.

faqs.q: What percentage of income does this replace?
faqs.a: Most policies replace 50-75% of your monthly income, up to a maximum monthly benefit (typically ₦1M-₦2M).

faqs.q: How long is the waiting period before benefits start?
faqs.a: Common deferred periods are 30, 60, 90, or 180 days. Longer waiting periods mean lower premiums.

name: Fire Insurance
description: Standalone fire insurance covering the building structure only against fire, lightning, and explosion risks. Ideal for property owners and real estate investors.
common_risks: Loss of rental income after fire
exclusions: Contents and equipment inside the building
Storm, flood, earthquake (add Special Perils rider)
Wear and tear of building materials
claim_examples: A fire gutted a 4-story commercial building in Ikeja, building-only fire policy paid ₦35M for structural rebuilding
Lightning struck a residential building causing ₦2.5M in structural damage to the roof and electrical system

objections.objection: The tenant should insure the building
objections.response: Tenants typically insure their contents and business, not the building structure. As the property owner, the building is your asset to protect. Most mortgage lenders also require building insurance.

objections.objection: Fire insurance is too narrow
objections.response: You're right—that's why we recommend upgrading to Fire & Special Perils which adds storm, flood, earthquake, and other risks for a small additional premium. For budget-conscious clients, Fire Insurance is a good starting point.

proposal_template: We recommend Fire Insurance for {{propertyName}} located at {{propertyAddress}} with a sum insured of ₦{{buildingValue}}. Estimated premium: ₦{{minPremium}} - ₦{{maxPremium}} annually.

faqs.q: Is fire insurance the same as homeowners insurance?
faqs.a: No. Fire insurance covers only the building structure against fire. Homeowners insurance is a broader package covering building, contents, and liability.

faqs.q: Do I need a valuation before insuring?
faqs.a: Yes, we recommend a professional valuation or at minimum a rebuild cost assessment to ensure adequate sum insured and avoid average clause penalties.
